grh_c3fe458a85a035bce771.title: Joe Perino
paragraphs: Dr. Christian is surprised one evening when Rivers End residents gather to introduce a successful visitor named Joe Perino, a man the doctor knew years earlier in Chicago. The meeting brings back the story of Joe as a delinquent boy arrested with a gang after a jewelry-store robbery. Although a judge is ready to send him to reform school, Dr. Christian argues that Joe has never had a fair chance, assumes responsibility for him and persuades the court to suspend sentence. He then convinces the very jeweler who was robbed to take Joe as an unpaid apprentice, even offering to guarantee any loss himself. The trust works. Joe learns the watch trade, eventually goes into business for himself and becomes successful. Now grown, he has tracked down the doctor who once believed in him and repays that faith on a scale no one expects: he donates $100,000 to build the modern Rivers End hospital Dr. Christian has long dreamed of, asking that it bear the doctors name.

grh_c340e20d3fdd8816465f.title: The Haunting of Sherlock Holmes
paragraphs: While recuperating in the Balkan kingdom of Grosneh, Holmes sees opera singer Lily Rayner arrested as a spy and apparently executed by firing squad. Her ghost then appears in his hotel room, prompting him to investigate secret passages and the evidence against her. The supposed espionage letters were in a language Lily could not speak and had been planted by her dresser Marta, who would inherit Lily's estate and lose that fortune if Lily married. Holmes recreates the ghostly visitation and tricks Marta into confessing. Lily then emerges alive: sympathetic officials had staged her execution with blank cartridges, and she used the haunting to draw Holmes into proving her innocence.
